reuse.why: There was no existing link-ownership helper to reuse; the new check uses the db layer directly and the existing link functions are reused unchanged, though the provider type is hand-assembled instead of taken from the account entity type.

duplication.why: The rule is written once in assertBankAccountIsNotLinked, but it is wrapped by five one-line per-provider assert*Available functions and five near-identical registration lambdas that differ only in the provider and the field holding the account id.

placement.why: The check is bolted onto the app.method registrations rather than living in the link path itself (the per-provider link functions or a shared link step), so the guard is detached from the code that writes the link and any other caller of linkXAccount skips it.

scope.why: Only the guard, its registration and a test.

maintainability.why: One SQL definition of 'linked' is easy to change, but the five pass-through wrappers and inline lambdas (one unformatted) add boilerplate a maintainer must keep in step with each new provider.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No existing abstraction for the rule is bypassed; the handlers' own link functions are still called.

disguised_duplication.where: assertGoCardlessAccountAvailable / assertSimpleFinAccountAvailable / assertPluggyAiAccountAvailable / assertAkahuAccountAvailable / assertEnableBankingAccountAvailable in server/accounts/app.ts are renamed copies of the same delegation, repeated again in the five registration lambdas.

one_place.where: assertBankAccountIsNotLinked in server/accounts/app.ts holds the single definition (same provider, same account id, not deleted, not the upgrading account), used by all five link handlers.
